critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict: Better than round 5 in the places Codex named, and still not at fern's level. The wide's crushed blacks are down to 6.6% below 8/255 (7.9% at 8 or below), from 10.9% for the round-5 wide on the same fixed grade. It was about 30% before the grade fix, so most of that larger drop came from the grade. The glazing, the counter row and the back wall now hold detail. The agent now types with both hands, curved, on the keyboard, which reads at once in the profile. The trolley rebuild also landed: a tube push frame with a brake bar over a solid deck, which reads as a luggage trolley. But the one beat this stage exists for, Dawn handing over her passport, still does not read in the reverse, the shot meant to carry it. The booklet showed whole in round 5. Raising the shoulder aim from 1.32 to 1.355 (round 5's fix for the steel nosing) pushed it off the bottom of the frame. Only a pale mauve-grey sliver about 18 px tall is left at the bottom edge. Her hand sits at that edge with spread fingers pointing almost straight at the lens: still a claw pressing a counter, not a hand sliding a booklet across. Two round-5 P2s were attempted and fell short. The hand flag is in the scene, but in the reverse the hand is still hotter than her face: graded median about 165 on the hand (about 173 on its back) against about 155 on the forehead. In the profile the back of her hand peaks at about 224, the brightest pixels in the frame. The monitor was cut from 5.0 to 3.0 and fell from about 190 to about 172 graded, but it is still the largest bright surface in the profile, sitting between the two people. The scale close-up was reframed (42 mm, camera pulled back so the plate sits inside the frame), but it reads much as before: about 30% dark floor and wall to the right of the display post, a dark counter-end slab across the left fifth, and now slices of Dawn's hand and pale calf cut by the left edge. The case's front matches across cameras (graded 25-32). In the profile, though, its display-lit side reads slate blue-grey (about 58 against about 30 on the duffel), so it looks like a lighter bag. The hair is still faceted, with a stepped shell above the ear. The wide's brightest large shape is still the blank lightbox sign directly above the counter, not the exchange. These are mostly 6s with a 5 on the story beat they exist for.
answers: 1) Does the gesture read as passing a passport in the reverse? No. Contact is now real: the pads land on the booklet and leave small contact shadows, and at 4x zoom I see no gap. But three problems kill the read. (a) The passport is almost out of frame. Only a strip about 18 px tall shows along the bottom edge (y about 702-720). It is mauve in the raw frame and nearly grey after the grade, with no visible thickness, page block or outline, so it reads as a patch on the counter. In round 5 it showed whole; raising the aim from 1.32 to 1.355 cut it off. (b) The hand is posed to press, not to pass. The four fingers point almost straight at the lens and drop steeply from knuckles held high above the booklet. They are spread apart, their tips face the lens and the thumb is hidden. That is a claw or a piano chord. A hand handing something over lies flatter, with the fingers together and the pads on the booklet's trailing (Dawn-side) half, pushing it toward the agent. (c) The hand is the hottest skin in the frame (graded median about 165, against about 155 on the forehead) and it sits at the bottom edge of the frame, so the eye lands on a cut-off white hand. In the profile the same gesture half-reads: a hand flat on the high ledge over a thin pale-grey slab only a few pixels thick, which does not read as a passport at 1280 px. The back of that hand peaks at graded about 224, the hottest point in the frame. 2) Do the baggage scale and duffel read together? In the wide, yes, and well: the duffel in front, the case behind, both on the raised plate, the display on its post at the plate's corner and the belt walls behind. In the scale close-up they read as sitting on one plate, but only as silhouettes. The duffel (graded about 30) and the case front (about 27) are near-black on a lighter steel plate (about 55-80). The faces toward the display are no brighter than their shadow sides (raw: the duffel's right end is 17 against 23 on its left end; the case's right edge is 19 against 20 on its left). After the display and its post, the plate and its rim are the brightest structure. The display stands off to the right on its post with about 30% dark floor and wall beyond it, so the frame reads as 'bags, and a screen over there' rather than one weighing unit. Slivers of Dawn's hand and calf are cut by the left edge. In the profile both bags sit on the scale. The case's front matches the close-up (graded about 25), but its display-facing side reads slate blue-grey (about 58), much lighter than the duffel, so it looks like a lighter bag than the one in the close-up. 3) Does the terminal have enough depth without taking attention off the exchange? Depth: enough. The counter row recedes left, the glazing and the apron lights read, a column frames the left edge, and the back wall now holds panels. Attention: not yet. The blank overhead sign panel (graded median about 85, a flat lightbox) is the largest bright shape in the frame and sits right above the counter. The chrome queue posts are the highest-contrast forms in the left half (highlights up to 230), and the nearest one is planted at the bottom centre. The exchange itself fills about 110 x 230 px. Its brightest notes are the two heads (Dawn's crown at p95 about 186, the agent's face about 171), and Dawn's bare calves (about 115-140) are as large and nearly as pale, which pulls the eye down to her legs. A soft haze column (graded about 45 against 27-33 on either side) falls from the bulkhead straight onto the open desk. It leads the eye to the exchange, so it can stay. The bottom third is dark floor (median about 34), broken only by the queue posts and the trolley.

fixes.problem: The passport is cut off by the bottom of the frame: an 18 px pale sliver. It showed whole in round 5, before the aim was raised from 1.32 to 1.355. The hand reads as a spread claw pointing at the lens, so the reverse does not show a passport being handed over.
fixes.fix: Tilt the shoulder camera down: lower the aim z from 1.355 to about 1.295 (about 1.7 deg, roughly 55 px). The counter top then fills the bottom 17-18% of the frame, and the headroom above her hair drops from about 115 px to about 60 px. If the agent-side steel nosing comes back into frame, keep it at least 25 px inside the bottom edge (round 5's other option). Keep the existing booklet. It is already built in three layers, a back, a cream page block and a front (128 x 90 mm, about 6 mm thick, nothing printed), and it is already yawed 18 deg off the lens, so it needs no rebuild and no turn. In pose_cast, set its offset from the solved pads about 1-1.5 cm further toward the agent (+Y): location.y = pad.y + about 0.03 instead of + 0.017. The pads then sit 10-20 mm in from the booklet's Dawn-side edge, on its trailing half, and its agent-side edge stays at least 2 cm short of the ledge edge. Re-pose the hand to push it. In rest_hand, use curl about 8 and set the per-finger spreads (now -3/-1/1/3) to 0. Let the wrist drop so the MCP knuckles sit 12-15 mm above the cover, and lay the thumb along the booklet's frame-left side (her inner side). Optionally, turn fwd_dir 15-20 deg further inward so the fingers are not aimed straight at the lens. Check: at least 70% of the booklet's outline is visible, 40 px or more inside the bottom edge, and the fingers read as a flat hand at 3x zoom.

fixes.problem: The brightness hierarchy is still wrong, although both round-5 fixes are in the scene. Shoulder: the hand (graded median about 165, about 173 on its back) is hotter than the forehead (about 155). Profile: the back of the same hand peaks at about 224, the hottest point in the frame. The monitor face (median about 172, down from about 190 after the 5.0 to 3.0 cut) is still the largest bright surface, and it sits between the two people.
fixes.fix: Hand: the hand flag (0.28 x 0.21 m at x0 + 0.30, y 0.12, z 1.95) sits in the island key's path to the hand. The stronger 180 W down_front strip at y 0.45 reaches the hand past it: its path crosses z 1.95 near y 0.26, beyond the flag's edge at 0.225. Lower the flag to about z 1.55 (0.5 m above the ledge), where both paths cross it. Slide it in Y until the shoulder hand reads graded 135-145, below the forehead, and the profile hand's p95 is 190 or less, with the face unchanged. Monitor: cut the screen emission again, from 3.0 to about 1.8, and keep desk0_mon_light at 6 W, so the screen's graded median is 115-125 in the profile. Re-measure both.

fixes.problem: The blank overhead sign panel (graded about 85) is the largest bright shape in the frame and sits directly above the counter. The chrome queue posts are the highest-contrast forms in the lower left, and the nearest one stands at the bottom centre. Both pull the eye away from the exchange.
fixes.fix: Cut sign_on's strength again, from 0.55 to about 0.22, so the lit sign reads graded 45-55, below the stone skin. Change the queue posts from 'polished steel' to a satin finish (roughness 0.35-0.45, base colour about 0.35), so their reflections drop under 150 graded. Optionally, go from 24 mm to about 28 mm and lower the camera about 0.3 m. The counter-and-scale group then grows from about a third of the frame width toward 40%, and the bottom third holds less floor. Keep every queue post wholly in or wholly out of frame.

fixes.problem: The camera was reframed this round (42 mm, pulled back so the plate sits inside the frame), but the composition reads as before. About 30% of the width is dark floor and wall right of the display post, and a dark counter-end slab fills the left fifth. Dawn's hand and calf are now cut by the left edge. The bags read as near-black silhouettes (case front about 27, duffel about 30) on a lighter plate. Their faces toward the display are no brighter than their shadow sides, although round 5's re-aim of disp_light (18 W, aimed at xs + 0.15, 0.45, 0.45) is already in.
fixes.fix: The group already fills about 86% of the frame height (display top near y 70, plate rim near y 690), so a longer lens alone would crop the display or the plate. Lower the camera from z 1.24 to about 0.95 and re-aim at the group's centre. The plate then foreshortens, which frees roughly 10% of the height, so the lens can go to about 46-48 mm. Check that the plate's front rim stays 25 px or more inside the bottom edge and the display head stays inside the top. Hide Dawn from this camera, or pan until no part of her is within 60 px of the left edge. For the bags, raise disp_light from 18 W to about 35-40 W inside its link. If the duffel's right end and the case's right edge still do not lift, add a small unseen cool card low at frame right, light-linked to the bags only and aimed at those faces. Target raw 40-50 on those faces, clearly above their shadow sides, with the display still the brightest thing. Do this together with the case fix below, because the same light lifts the case's side in the profile.

fixes.problem: In the profile the case's display-facing side reads slate blue-grey (graded about 58, raw 61), against about 25 on its own front and 28-34 on the duffel. The scale close-up shows only its dark front (about 27), so the case reads as a lighter bag in the profile. Its sidewall strip also reads light in the wide.
fixes.fix: That side is lit by the display's light-linked fill. The duffel is loaded at val 0.25, a quarter of its source value, while the case keeps the default val 1.0 (sat 0.6), so under the same light the case reads much lighter. Keep the case in the display's link (the scale fix needs that light) and lower it to about val 0.5 and sat 0.35. Target: its lit side reads graded about 40-45 in the profile, still visibly lit by the display but the same charcoal bag, and its front reads graded 25-32 in all three cameras.

fixes.problem: The ledge top in the reverse shows big, soft, cloudy blotches at the frame's most important edge. It looks like a stained or marbled slab rather than a dark solid surface.
fixes.fix: The blotches match pbr()'s smudge patches. On 'dark solid surface', smudge=0.08 drops the roughness from 0.48-0.59 to 0.08 in world-space patches about 30 cm across (noise scale 3), and those glossy patches mirror the lit hall. Raise this material's smudge target to about 0.38-0.42, or drop smudge from it, so the ledge reads as one dark surface with a soft, even sheen. Re-check the bottom of the reverse at 2x zoom.

fixes.problem: Shared kit: the sculpted hair is a faceted shell with hard stepped bands above the ear (shoulder), and the bun still reads as a ball stuck on the back of the head (profile).
fixes.fix: Round 5's request is partly in code: sculpt_hair in checkin_hall.py now adds a level-1 subdivision and squashes the bun to 0.78 x 0.84, but neither change shows in these frames. Ask Codex to check that the hair mesh is shade-smooth (the bands look like flat-shaded strips), raise the subdivision to 2 and sink the bun about 30% into the head. Then move the change into people.py so every scene shares it. Re-check the side of the head at 3x zoom in the shoulder frame.

fixes.problem: Dawn's hanging right hand in the profile is stiff, with slightly spread pale fingers.
fixes.fix: Set its curl to 15-18 with the fingers together and the thumb against the side of the index finger.
